Katana's unique combination of 35-second speed AND ghost recovery + unallocated carving + automated triage questions creates an uncontested position.

## 2.3 Feature Parity Analysis

### Table Stakes (Must Have)

Features customers expect from any forensic artifact analysis tool in 2026:

| Feature | Why Expected | Our Implementation |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| E01/raw disk image support | E01 is the dominant forensic image format; practitioners will not extract artifacts manually | EWF decompression via libewf FFI, MBR/GPT partition detection, NTFS auto-discovery |
| USN Journal parsing (V2/V3/V4) | Core artifact — every NTFS forensic tool must parse this | Streaming parser with parallel chunk processing via rayon; handles V2, V3, and V4 records |
| MFT parsing and correlation | Path resolution requires MFT; standalone USN parsing without paths is nearly useless | Full MFT record parsing with entry/sequence matching, $SI/$FN timestamp extraction |
| Multiple output formats | Practitioners have diverse downstream workflows (Timeline Explorer, mactime, SOAR, databases) | 7 formats: CSV (MFTECmd-compatible), JSONL, SQLite, Body (mactime), TLN, XML, HTML report |
| Cross-platform support | Analysts use macOS, Linux, and Windows; Windows-only tools exclude half the community | Pure Rust — compiles natively for macOS, Linux, Windows from the same codebase |

### Differentiators (Where We Win)

Features or approaches that set Security Ronin Katana apart:

| Differentiator | Competitors' Approach | Our Approach | Why It Matters |
|----------------|----------------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Ghost record recovery** | No competitor recovers USN records from $LogFile transaction pages | Extract USN records embedded in $LogFile RESTART/RECORD pages that never appeared in $UsnJrnl:$J | Recovers file activity evidence that attackers thought they destroyed by clearing the journal. 771 ghost records found on Szechuan Sauce CTF image that MFTECmd missed entirely |
| **Unallocated space carving** | Most tools only read allocated artifacts; X-Ways has manual carving but no automated USN/MFT carving | Automated carving of USN record structures and MFT entries from unallocated clusters | Recovers evidence from disk space the OS considers empty. Catches attacker cleanup that overwrote original artifact locations |
| **Zero-UNKNOWN path resolution** | MFTECmd produces 40%+ UNKNOWN paths when MFT entries are reused; other tools show raw MFT entry numbers | CyberCX Rewind algorithm: reverse-chronological journal traversal resolves paths through entry reuse chains | Every record has a full file path. No manual correlation needed. Investigation narratives can be written directly from output |
| **12 automated IR triage questions** | No competitor provides automated incident response question answering from USN journal data | 12 pattern-matched triage questions across 4 tiers (what happened, how bad, still at risk, covered tracks) with evidence counts | Practitioner gets the answers an incident commander needs in 35 seconds instead of building them manually over 45-90 minutes |
| **QuadLink 4-artifact correlation** | Tools parse artifacts in isolation; correlation is manual | Cross-reference $UsnJrnl + $MFT + $LogFile + $MFTMirr in a single pass with provenance tagging | Most complete picture of file system activity from a single command. Detects MFT tampering via mirror comparison |
| **35-second wall-clock triage** | AXIOM: hours for full analysis. X-Ways: minutes to hours. Velociraptor: minutes for VQL queries after collection | Rust memory-mapped I/O, rayon parallel chunk processing, streaming pipeline. 35s on 40GB E01 with 847K records | Speed is not a marketing claim — it is a benchmarked, CI-validated performance guarantee on specific hardware and dataset |

### Gaps (Where Competitors Win)

Honest assessment of where competitors are stronger:

| Gap | Competitor Advantage | Our Mitigation | Priority to Address |
|-----|---------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Artifact breadth** | AXIOM parses 800+ artifact types (event logs, registry, browser, mobile). Katana parses NTFS journal artifacts only | Phase 2 roadmap adds event logs, prefetch, registry, shimcache. Phase 1 focuses on being best-in-class at one artifact family | Medium — address in Phase 2 after revenue validation |
| **GUI visualization** | AXIOM, X-Ways, and Autopsy offer interactive GUI for visual analysis. Timeline Explorer provides tabular filtering | HTML report with Story + Explore tabs is the GUI. No desktop application | Low — CLI users prefer terminal; HTML report satisfies visual analysis needs |
| **Remote collection** | Velociraptor, Binalyze AIR, and CrowdStrike collect artifacts remotely from live endpoints | Phase 2 Velociraptor integration as import source; Phase 3 targeted collection agent | High — critical for MSSP workflow; Velociraptor integration in Phase 2 |
| **Mobile forensics** | AXIOM and Cellebrite handle phone extractions alongside computer forensics | Not on roadmap. NTFS journal triage and mobile forensics are different domains | Low — not our market; refer practitioners to Cellebrite/AXIOM for mobile |
| **Team collaboration** | Timesketch, Binalyze AIR, and AXIOM Cyber offer multi-analyst investigation workflows | Phase 3 roadmap: web-based report viewer, team annotations, RBAC | Medium — address after solo-practitioner adoption proves the engine |

## 2.4 Novelty Validation (Research-Backed)

> **Last Validated**: 2026-03-10
> **Method**: Analysis of DFIR tool landscape across open-source repositories, commercial product documentation, SANS course materials, conference presentations (SANS DFIR Summit, OSDFCon, DFRWS), and practitioner community discussions (DFIR Discord, Reddit r/computerforensics, forensic-focused Slack channels).

### Research Conclusion

> Security Ronin Katana is a **competitive differentiation play with category-creation elements**. Individual capabilities exist in isolation across the market (USN parsing in MFTECmd, carving in X-Ways, collection in KAPE, timeline analysis in Timesketch), but no tool combines ghost record recovery, unallocated carving, zero-UNKNOWN path resolution, and automated IR triage questions in a single 35-second CLI execution. The novelty is in the integrated pipeline and the triage-question abstraction layer, not any single parsing capability.

### What Exists Today (Validated)

| Category | Examples | What They Offer | What They Lack |
|----------|----------|-----------------|----------------|
| USN Journal parsers | MFTECmd, usn.py, ntfs-linker | Parse allocated USN journal records; MFTECmd is fastest and most popular | No ghost recovery from $LogFile, no unallocated carving, 40%+ UNKNOWN paths on reused MFT entries, no automated triage questions |
| Full forensic suites | X-Ways, EnCase, Magnet AXIOM | Broad artifact coverage, GUI visualization, established vendor support | Slow (hours for full analysis), expensive ($850-$15K/yr), closed-source, no automated IR questions from USN data |
| Collection tools | KAPE, Velociraptor, Binalyze AIR | Fast triage collection from live endpoints; KAPE targets + modules pattern | Collection only — analysis requires separate downstream tools; no integrated triage question answering |
| Timeline analysis | Timesketch, Plaso/log2timeline | Collaborative timeline with search and tagging; OpenSearch-backed scalability | Requires pre-processed input; heavy infrastructure; no artifact parsing or evidence recovery built in |
| Carving tools | Scalpel, PhotoRec, X-Ways carving | File carving from unallocated space by signature/header matching | General-purpose carving — no USN record structure awareness, no MFT entry carving, no forensic triage integration |

### What's Novel in Security Ronin Katana

| Innovation | Why Novel | Competitive Implication |
|------------|-----------|------------------------|
| **Ghost record recovery from $LogFile** | No publicly available tool extracts USN records from NTFS $LogFile transaction pages. $LogFile contains USN records from pending transactions that may never appear in $UsnJrnl:$J. This is a forensically significant evidence source that the entire market ignores | First-mover advantage in an evidence recovery technique. Competitors would need to reverse-engineer $LogFile transaction page structures to replicate. Academic papers exist on $LogFile structure but no tool implements USN extraction from it |
| **Integrated triage-question abstraction** | Every existing tool outputs raw data (parsed records, timelines, CSV rows). No tool maps forensic artifacts to incident response questions automatically. The 12-question framework translates file system activity into the language incident commanders use | Creates a new interaction paradigm: "ask questions, get answers" vs. "parse data, build your own analysis." Competitors would need to build both the question framework AND the precision/recall validation methodology |
| **Zero-UNKNOWN path resolution through Rewind** | CyberCX published the Rewind algorithm concept, but no open-source tool implements it completely with unallocated and ghost record integration | Eliminates the most common complaint about MFTECmd (40%+ UNKNOWN paths). Once practitioners experience zero-UNKNOWN output, going back to partial path resolution is unacceptable |
| **QuadLink 4-artifact correlation in a single pass** | Tools parse $UsnJrnl, $MFT, $LogFile, and $MFTMirr independently. No tool cross-references all four in a single execution with provenance tagging per record | Produces the most complete picture of NTFS file system activity possible from a single command. The provenance tag (allocated journal, ghost from $LogFile, carved from unallocated) is forensically meaningful metadata no other tool provides |

### Positioning Shorthand

For market/pitch purposes:

> "Think of it as MFTECmd's analysis depth meets KAPE's collection speed — but it also recovers the evidence attackers deleted, answers 12 IR questions automatically, and resolves every file path to zero unknowns. One Rust binary, 35 seconds, Apache-2.0."

A VC-funded forensic tool must show MRR growth, which incentivizes feature-checkbox development, enterprise-only pricing, and marketing spend over engineering quality. The open-core model with revenue from 50 paying enterprise customers is sustainable without external capital. Stay bootstrapped until product-market fit is proven |
| **Add mobile forensics** | AXIOM and Cellebrite handle both computer and mobile. Practitioners doing IR often need both | Mobile forensics is a fundamentally different domain (extraction methods, artifact types, OS structures, legal frameworks). Adding mobile would violate the "depth over breadth" belief and compete with established tools (Cellebrite, AXIOM) in a market where they have decade-long head starts. Partner with mobile tools via structured output export, don't build one |

# Security Ronin Katana: Accessibility Strategy

Source: https://github.com/securityronin/usnjrnl-forensic/blob/main/north-star-advisor/docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY.md

# Security Ronin Katana: Accessibility Strategy

> **Parent**: [USER_JOURNEYS.md](USER_JOURNEYS.md)
> **Related**: [UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md](UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)
> **Generation Step**: 5c of 13 -- Requires `journeys.*`
> **Created**: 2026-03-10
> **Status**: Draft
> **WCAG Target**: 2.1 Level AA

Comprehensive accessibility patterns for Security Ronin Katana's three rendering surfaces: CLI terminal output, self-contained HTML reports, and enterprise web dashboard. This document covers NO_COLOR compliance for CLI, WCAG 2.1 AA for HTML/web, screen reader patterns for real-time WebSocket collaboration, and color-blind safe severity indicators across all surfaces.

## Document Purpose

Security Ronin Katana serves forensic analysts across three distinct rendering surfaces, each with unique accessibility requirements:

| Surface | Tier | Technology | Primary A11y Concern |
|---------|------|------------|---------------------|
| **CLI terminal output** | Community + Enterprise | Rust `colored` crate, ANSI escapes | NO_COLOR compliance, screen reader text, pipe detection |
| **HTML report** | Community + Enterprise | Static HTML/CSS/JS generated by Rust | WCAG 2.1 AA, offline self-contained, semantic markup |
| **Enterprise web UI** | Enterprise only | Axum + Askama + vanilla CSS + WebSocket | Full WCAG 2.1 AA, real-time collaboration a11y |

Forensic analysts work long analysis sessions (12-16 hours during incident response) in high-pressure scenarios where cognitive fatigue is a real safety concern. Accessibility is not an afterthought -- it is a trust requirement aligned with Axiom 4 (Open Core Trust > Revenue Extraction) and a foundation for analyst effectiveness.

**Relationship to Other Documents:**
- **UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md** defines the color tokens verified against WCAG AA contrast ratios
- **USER_JOURNEYS.md** defines the journey phases referenced for focus management and error recovery
- **NORTHSTAR_EXTRACT.md** provides the axioms that govern accessibility priorities
- **This document** provides comprehensive patterns, testing protocols, and implementation guidance

## 0. CLI Accessibility

CLI is the primary interface for community users and the foundation for all tiers. Since CLI output is inherently keyboard-operated, the accessibility focus is on visual output adaptability and screen reader compatibility.

### 0.1 NO_COLOR Compliance

Security Ronin Katana respects the [NO_COLOR standard](https://no-color.org/) and related environment signals. The `colored` crate in Rust handles most of this, but the implementation must enforce these rules:

```rust
// src/output/color.rs

/// Color suppression priority (checked in order):
/// 1. --no-color CLI flag (explicit user request)
/// 2. NO_COLOR environment variable (any value, including empty string)
/// 3. TERM=dumb (terminal does not support escape sequences)
/// 4. Non-TTY stdout (piping to file, grep, or another tool)
///
/// When color is suppressed:
/// - Strip ALL ANSI escape sequences from output
/// - Severity indicators use text prefixes: [CRITICAL], [HIGH], [MEDIUM], [LOW], [INFO]
/// - Ghost recovery entries use prefix: [GHOST]
/// - Progress bars use ASCII: [=====>    ] 60%
/// - Structure uses indentation and dashes, not color

fn should_use_color(args: &CliArgs) -> bool {
    if args.no_color {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var("NO_COLOR").is_ok() {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var("TERM").map(|t| t == "dumb").unwrap_or(false) {
        return false;
    }
    if !atty::is(atty::Stream::Stdout) {
        return false;
    }
    true
}
```

### 0.2 ANSI Color Fallback Strategy

Terminals vary in color depth support. Katana uses a tiered fallback:

| Terminal Capability | Detection | Color Strategy |
|--------------------|-----------|--------------------|
| 24-bit (truecolor) | `COLORTERM=truecolor` | Full design token hex colors |
| 256-color | `TERM` contains `256color` | Closest 256-color approximation |
| 16-color (basic) | Default TTY | ANSI 16-color severity mapping |
| No color | `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, non-TTY | Text-only severity prefixes |

**16-color severity mapping (from UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM):**

| Severity | ANSI Code | Visual | Text Fallback |
|----------|-----------|--------|---------------|
| Critical | `\x1b[1;91m` (bold bright red) | Bright red, bold | `[CRITICAL]` |
| High | `\x1b[91m` (bright red) | Bright red | `[HIGH]` |
| Medium | `\x1b[93m` (bright yellow) | Bright yellow | `[MEDIUM]` |
| Low | `\x1b[96m` (bright cyan) | Bright cyan | `[LOW]` |
| Info | `\x1b[37m` (white) | White | `[INFO]` |
| Ghost | `\x1b[35m` (magenta) | Magenta | `[GHOST]` |

### 0.3 Screen Reader Compatible CLI Output

When output is consumed by screen readers (common when analysts use terminal emulators with assistive technology), the structure must be parseable as plain text:

```
=== TRIAGE RESULTS: case-2026-0310 ===

Evidence: laptop.E01
Processing time: 34.2 seconds
Records parsed: 1,247,832
Ghost records recovered: 14,207

--- Question 1: Was endpoint protection disabled? ---
Answer: YES (confidence: HIGH)
Severity: CRITICAL
Evidence:
  [1] 2026-03-08T14:23:17Z DELETE Windows Defender\MpCmdRun.exe
  [2] 2026-03-08T14:23:19Z DELETE Windows Defender\MsMpEng.exe
  [3] 2026-03-08T14:23:22Z RENAME Windows Defender\Platform\ -> .bak

--- Question 2: Was there evidence of lateral movement? ---
Answer: NO
Severity: INFO
Evidence: No matching USN journal entries found.
```

**Key principles for screen reader output:**
- Use consistent section delimiters (`===` for headers, `---` for questions)
- Prefix every severity with text label, not just color
- Number evidence entries for reference
- Use standard date/time formats (ISO 8601)
- Avoid Unicode box-drawing characters in default mode (use `--unicode` flag to opt in)
- Always include counts in plain text (not embedded in progress bars)

### 0.4 Pipe-Safe Output

When stdout is not a TTY (detected via `atty::is()`), Katana automatically:

1. **Strips ANSI escape sequences** -- no color codes in piped output
2. **Removes progress bars** -- no carriage returns or cursor manipulation
3. **Uses machine-parseable delimiters** -- tab-separated or JSON lines
4. **Preserves semantic structure** -- headers, evidence blocks, severity labels remain as text

```bash
# Human-readable (TTY)
katana triage laptop.E01

# Machine-parseable (pipe)
katana triage laptop.E01 | grep "CRITICAL"

# Explicit JSON output for tooling
katana triage laptop.E01 --format jsonl
```

### 0.5 Progress Bar Degradation

```
TTY mode:
[=================>          ] 67% Parsing USN records...

Non-TTY mode:
[INFO] Parsing USN records: 25% complete
[INFO] Parsing USN records: 50% complete
[INFO] Parsing USN records: 75% complete
[INFO] Parsing USN records: 100% complete

TERM=dumb mode:
Parsing USN records: 25% complete
Parsing USN records: 50% complete
Parsing USN records: 75% complete
Parsing USN records: 100% complete
```

### 0.6 CLI Error Output

Errors always go to stderr with clear, parseable formatting. Every error follows the three-part pattern: what happened, why, and what to do.

```
ERROR: Failed to mount evidence image.
Reason: EWF file signature invalid at offset 0x0.
Action: Verify the file is a valid E01/EWF image. Run 'katana verify laptop.E01' to check integrity.
```

## 2. Color Contrast Verification

All color pairings verified against WCAG AA minimum contrast ratios.

### 2.1 Dark Theme (Default)

| Foreground | Background | Hex Pair | Contrast Ratio | Passes AA | Usage |
|------------|------------|----------|----------------|-----------|-------|
| `--text-primary` | `--bg` | `#e6edf3` on `#0d1117` | **13.2:1** | Yes (AA+AAA) | Body text |
| `--text-secondary` | `--bg` | `#9da5b4` on `#0d1117` | **7.0:1** | Yes (AA+AAA) | Labels, metadata |
| `--text-muted` | `--bg` | `#545d68` on `#0d1117` | **3.1:1** | Large text only | Decorative labels, timestamps with adjacent context |
| `--accent` | `--bg` | `#58a6ff` on `#0d1117` | **5.3:1** | Yes | Links, interactive elements |
| `--critical` | `--bg` | `#ff7b72` on `#0d1117` | **5.5:1** | Yes | Critical severity |
| `--high` | `--bg` | `#ffa657` on `#0d1117` | **7.3:1** | Yes | High severity |
| `--warning/medium` | `--bg` | `#d29922` on `#0d1117` | **5.8:1** | Yes | Medium severity |
| `--low/info-accent` | `--bg` | `#58a6ff` on `#0d1117` | **5.3:1** | Yes | Low severity |
| `--info` | `--bg` | `#8b949e` on `#0d1117` | **5.5:1** | Yes | Info severity |
| `--ghost` | `--bg` | `#bc8cff` on `#0d1117` | **5.9:1** | Yes | Ghost recovery |
| `--error` | `--bg` | `#f85149` on `#0d1117` | **4.9:1** | Yes | Error text |
| `--success` | `--bg` | `#3fb950` on `#0d1117` | **5.0:1** | Yes | Success/resolved |
| `--text-primary` | `--surface` | `#e6edf3` on `#161b22` | **11.1:1** | Yes | Card body text |
| `--text-secondary` | `--surface` | `#9da5b4` on `#161b22` | **5.8:1** | Yes | Card labels |
| `--border-strong` | `--bg` | `#484f58` on `#0d1117` | **3.2:1** | Yes (non-text) | Interactive borders |

> **Note**: Muted text (#545d68) at 3.1:1 fails AA for normal text. Usage is restricted to decorative labels and timestamps where adjacent context provides the information. For any standalone muted text, use #9da5b4 (secondary) instead.

### 2.3 Colorblind Safety Matrix

Color must never be the sole conveyor of meaning. Every color-coded element has a redundant signal.

| Element | Color Signal | Redundant Signal | Deuteranopia Safe | Protanopia Safe | Tritanopia Safe |
|---------|-------------|------------------|-------------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Triage YES badge | Green `#3fb950` | Text "YES" + checkmark icon | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Triage NO badge | Neutral `#8b949e` | Text "NO" | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Triage CRITICAL badge | Red `#ff7b72` | Text "YES" + shield-alert icon + bold border | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: Critical | Red `#ff7b72` | `[!!]` symbol + "CRITICAL" text + solid fill badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: High | Orange `#ffa657` | `[!]` symbol + "HIGH" text + solid fill badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: Medium | Yellow `#d29922` | `[~]` symbol + "MEDIUM" text + outline badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: Low | Blue `#58a6ff` | `[-]` symbol + "LOW" text + outline badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: Info | Gray `#8b949e` | `[.]` symbol + "INFO" text + no badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Severity: Ghost | Purple `#bc8cff` | `[G]` symbol + "GHOST" text + dashed badge | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Stat card: Total | Blue `#58a6ff` | Label "Total Records" + position (first card) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Stat card: Carved | Purple `#bc8cff` | Label "Carved Records" + dagger icon | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Stat card: Ghost | Cyan `#39d4e0` | Label "Ghost Records" + ghost icon | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| WebSocket status | Green/red | Text "Connected"/"Disconnected" + icon shape | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Case status | Various | Text label + distinct icon per status | Yes | Yes | Yes |

### 2.4 Print Theme (Court Exhibits)

When the report is printed or `@media print` is active, colors invert to a light theme for legibility on paper and photocopies.

```css
@media print {
  body {
    background: #ffffff;
    color: #1a1a1a;
    font-size: 10pt;
  }

  .stat-card {
    background: #f5f5f5;
    border: 1px solid #333333;
    color: #1a1a1a;
  }

  .triage-card {
    background: #ffffff;
    border: 1px solid #333333;
    break-inside: avoid;
  }

  .triage-badge {
    border: 2px solid #1a1a1a;
    font-weight: 700;
  }

  .triage-badge.yes { background: #e6f4ea; color: #1a1a1a; }
  .triage-badge.no { background: #f5f5f5; color: #1a1a1a; }
  .triage-badge.critical { background: #fce8e6; color: #1a1a1a; }

  a { color: #1a1a1a; text-decoration: underline; }
  a::after { content: " (" attr(href) ")"; font-size: 8pt; }

  /* Hide interactive-only elements */
  .tab-btn, #tab-explore, .search-bar, .filter-bar { display: none; }

  /* Force Story tab visible */

```

**Court exhibit requirements:**
- All evidence data must be legible in grayscale photocopy
- Badge text (YES/NO/CRITICAL) readable without color
- Timestamps must include timezone designator
- Page header repeats case identifier and tool version

## 3. Screen Reader Patterns

Security Ronin Katana has three distinct screen reader contexts: CLI terminal output, static HTML reports, and real-time enterprise web UI with WebSocket collaboration.

### 3.1 HTML Report Landmarks

The HTML report uses semantic landmarks for efficient screen reader navigation.

```html
<body>
  <a class="skip-link" href="#triage-results">Skip to triage results</a>

  <header role="banner">
    <h1>Security Ronin Katana -- Triage Report</h1>
    <p>Case: <span>{{case_id}}</span> | Generated: <time>{{timestamp}}</time></p>
  </header>

  <main id="triage-results" role="main">
    <section aria-label="Evidence Summary Statistics">
      <div id="stat-cards" role="group" aria-label="Key metrics">
        <!-- Stat cards with individual aria-labels -->
      </div>
    </section>

    <nav aria-label="Report sections">
      <div role="tablist" aria-label="Report views">
        <button role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="tab-story" id="btn-story">
          Story
        </button>
        <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="tab-explore" id="btn-explore">
          Explore
        </button>
      </div>
    </nav>

    <section id="tab-story" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="btn-story">
      <!-- Triage question cards -->
    </section>

    <section id="tab-explore" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="btn-explore" hidden>
      <!-- Data table -->
    </section>
  </main>

  <footer role="contentinfo">
    <p>Generated by Security Ronin Katana v{{version}}</p>
  </footer>
</body>
```

### 3.2 Stat Cards

Each stat card announces its label and value together.

```html
<div class="stat-card"
     role="group"
     aria-label="Total Records: 142,847">
  <div class="label" aria-hidden="true">Total Records</div>
  <div class="value" aria-hidden="true">142,847</div>
</div>
```

Screen reader announces: "Total Records: 142,847, group"

### 3.3 Triage Question Cards

Each triage card is a self-contained unit with question, answer badge, confidence, and supporting evidence.

```html
<div class="triage-card"
     role="article"
     aria-label="Triage question: Were files securely deleted?">
  <div class="triage-header">
    <h3 id="triage-q1">Were files securely deleted?</h3>
    <span class="triage-badge yes"
          role="status"
          aria-label="Answer: Yes, confidence high">
      YES
    </span>
  </div>
  <div class="triage-detail" aria-describedby="triage-q1">
    <p>3 files matched secure deletion patterns...</p>
    <table aria-label="Supporting evidence for secure deletion finding">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">Timestamp</th>
          <th scope="col">File Path</th>
          <th scope="col">Pattern</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <!-- Evidence rows -->
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</div>
```

### 3.4 Explore Tab Data Table

The explore table contains potentially thousands of USN journal records. Screen reader support requires proper headers and navigation hints.

```html
<div role="region" aria-label="USN Journal records" tabindex="0">
  <div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" class="sr-only">
    <!-- Announces filter result count changes -->
    Showing 847 of 142,847 records
  </div>

  <table aria-label="USN Journal timeline">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col" aria-sort="descending">Timestamp</th>
        <th scope="col">File Path</th>
        <th scope="col">Reason Flags</th>
        <th scope="col">MFT Entry</th>
        <th scope="col">Source</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <!-- Data rows -->
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

### 3.5 Enterprise Web: Live Region Strategy for Real-Time Updates

The enterprise web UI has two distinct real-time update patterns: triage pipeline progress and WebSocket collaboration updates.

```html
<!-- Enterprise Web UI: Live region containers -->

<!-- Triage pipeline progress (polite -- non-urgent updates) -->
<div
  id="pipeline-status"
  role="status"
  aria-live="polite"
  aria-atomic="true"
  class="sr-only">
  <!-- Updated by JavaScript as pipeline stages complete -->
</div>

<!-- Collaboration activity (polite -- coalesced) -->
<div
  id="collab-activity"
  role="log"
  aria-live="polite"
  aria-atomic="false"
  aria-relevant="additions"
  class="sr-only">
  <!-- WebSocket messages appended here, coalesced to max 1 per 10 seconds -->
</div>

<!-- Error announcements (assertive -- immediate) -->
<div
  id="error-announcements"
  role="alert"
  aria-live="assertive"
  aria-atomic="true"
  class="sr-only">
  <!-- Pipeline failures, connection loss, permission errors -->
</div>

<!-- Triage completion (assertive -- milestone) -->
<div
  id="triage-complete"
  role="alert"
  aria-live="assertive"
  aria-atomic="true"
  class="sr-only">
  <!-- Announced when triage finishes -->
</div>
```

### 3.6 Pipeline Progress Announcements

The triage pipeline has defined stages. Announcements are coalesced to avoid overwhelming screen reader users during the ~35-second processing window:

```javascript
// enterprise/static/js/a11y.js

const PIPELINE_STAGES = [
  'Mounting evidence image',
  'Parsing USN journal',
  'Recovering ghost records',
  'Scanning unallocated space',
  'Reconstructing file paths',
  'Running triage questions',
  'Generating report'
];

// Coalesce: announce at most once per 5 seconds during pipeline
const MIN_ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL_MS = 5000;
let lastAnnounceTime = 0;

function announcePipelineProgress(stageIndex, totalStages) {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (now - lastAnnounceTime < MIN_ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL_MS) {
    return; // Skip to avoid overwhelming screen reader
  }
  lastAnnounceTime = now;

  const stage = PIPELINE_STAGES[stageIndex];
  const pipelineStatus = document.getElementById('pipeline-status');
  pipelineStatus.textContent =
    'Triage progress: step ' + (stageIndex + 1) + ' of ' + totalStages + '. ' + stage + '.';
}

function announcePipelineComplete(caseId, findingsCount, criticalCount) {
  const completeEl = document.getElementById('triage-complete');
  completeEl.textContent =
    'Triage complete for case ' + caseId + '. ' +
    findingsCount + ' findings identified, ' + criticalCount + ' critical. ' +
    'Results are now available.';
}

function announcePipelineError(errorMessage) {
  const errorEl = document.getElementById('error-announcements');
  errorEl.textContent = 'Triage error: ' + errorMessage + '. Check the error panel for details.';
}
```

### 3.7 WebSocket Collaboration Announcements

When multiple analysts collaborate on a case, WebSocket messages must be announced without creating a wall of noise:

```javascript
// enterprise/static/js/collab-a11y.js

const COLLAB_COALESCE_MS = 10000; // Announce at most once per 10 seconds
var collabBuffer = [];
var collabTimer = null;

function onCollabMessage(msg) {
  collabBuffer.push(msg);
  if (!collabTimer) {
    collabTimer = setTimeout(flushCollabAnnouncements, COLLAB_COALESCE_MS);
  }
}

function flushCollabAnnouncements() {
  collabTimer = null;
  if (collabBuffer.length === 0) return;

  var collabLog = document.getElementById('collab-activity');

  if (collabBuffer.length === 1) {
    var msg = collabBuffer[0];
    var announcement = document.createElement('div');
    announcement.textContent = formatCollabMessage(msg);
    collabLog.appendChild(announcement);
  } else {
    var summary = document.createElement('div');
    var analysts = [];
    collabBuffer.forEach(function(m) {
      if (analysts.indexOf(m.analyst) === -1) analysts.push(m.analyst);
    });
    summary.textContent =
      collabBuffer.length + ' collaboration updates from ' +
      analysts.length + ' analyst(s).';
    collabLog.appendChild(summary);
  }

  collabBuffer = [];

  // Prune old entries to prevent DOM growth
  while (collabLog.children.length > 20) {
    collabLog.removeChild(collabLog.firstChild);
  }
}

function formatCollabMessage(msg) {
  switch (msg.type) {
    case 'analyst_joined':
      return msg.analyst + ' joined the case.';
    case 'analyst_left':
      return msg.analyst + ' left the case.';
    case 'finding_added':
      return msg.analyst + ' added a ' + msg.severity + ' finding.';
    case 'note_added':
      return msg.analyst + ' added a note to question ' + msg.questionNumber + '.';
    case 'case_status_changed':
      return 'Case status changed to ' + msg.newStatus + ' by ' + msg.analyst + '.';
    default:
      return 'Case update from ' + msg.analyst + '.';
  }
}
```

### 3.8 Error Announcement Patterns

Errors across all surfaces follow a consistent three-part structure: what happened, what it means, and what to do next.

**CLI error output (screen reader friendly):**
```
ERROR: Failed to mount evidence image.
Reason: EWF file signature invalid at offset 0x0.
Action: Verify the file is a valid E01/EWF image. Run 'katana verify laptop.E01' to check integrity.
```

**HTML report error (embedded in static report):**
```html
<section role="alert" aria-label="Processing error">
  <h2>Triage Error</h2>
  <p><strong>Error:</strong> USN journal not found in NTFS volume.</p>
  <p><strong>Possible cause:</strong> The volume may not be NTFS, or the journal was deleted.</p>
  <p><strong>Suggested action:</strong> Verify the image contains an NTFS partition
    using <code>katana info image.E01</code>.</p>
</section>
```

**Enterprise web UI error (live region + focus management):**
```javascript
function announceError(error) {
  var errorEl = document.getElementById('error-announcements');
  errorEl.textContent =
    'Error: ' + error.summary + '. ' + error.suggestion + '. ' +
    'See the error panel for full details.';

  // Move focus to error panel for sighted keyboard users
  var errorPanel = document.getElementById('error-panel');
  if (errorPanel) {
    errorPanel.focus();
  }
}
```

## 4. Focus Management

### 4.1 Focus Strategy by Surface and State

| State | CLI | HTML Report | Enterprise Web |
|-------|-----|-------------|----------------|
| **Triage started** | N/A (blocking) | N/A (pre-generated) | Focus stays on "Start Triage" button; `aria-disabled="true"` applied |
| **Triage in progress** | Progress updates stream to stdout | N/A | Focus remains; pipeline status announced via live region |
| **Triage complete** | Results printed; cursor returns to prompt | N/A | Focus moves to results heading: `<h2 id="triage-results">` |
| **Triage error** | Error printed to stderr | Error section at top of report | Focus moves to error panel heading |
| **Case switch** | N/A (new command) | N/A (new report) | Focus moves to new case heading; previous case state preserved |
| **Modal open** | N/A | N/A | Focus trapped in modal; Esc or close button returns focus to trigger |
| **Analyst joins** | N/A | N/A | No focus change; polite live region announcement |

### 4.2 HTML Report Tab Navigation

The Story/Explore tabs implement the WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern with arrow key navigation.

```javascript
// Tab switching with keyboard
document.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]').forEach(function(tab) {
  tab.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
    var tabs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]'));
    var index = tabs.indexOf(e.target);

    if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowLeft') {
      e.preventDefault();
      var direction = e.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : -1;
      var next = (index + direction + tabs.length) % tabs.length;
      tabs[next].focus();
      tabs[next].click();
    }
  });
});
```

### 4.3 Enterprise Web Focus Implementation

```javascript
// enterprise/static/js/focus.js

/**
 * Focus management for triage completion.
 * Moves focus to results heading after pipeline completes.
 */
function onTriageComplete(caseId) {
  var resultsHeading = document.getElementById('triage-results');
  if (resultsHeading) {
    requestAnimationFrame(function() {
      resultsHeading.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      resultsHeading.focus();
      resultsHeading.addEventListener('blur', function handler() {
        resultsHeading.removeAttribute('tabindex');
        resultsHeading.removeEventListener('blur', handler);
      });
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Focus management for case switching.
 */
function onCaseSwitch(newCaseId) {
  var statusEl = document.getElementById('pipeline-status');
  statusEl.textContent = 'Switched to case ' + newCaseId + '.';

  var caseHeading = document.getElementById('case-heading-' + newCaseId);
  if (caseHeading) {
    caseHeading.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
    caseHeading.focus();
    caseHeading.addEventListener('blur', function handler() {
      caseHeading.removeAttribute('tabindex');
      caseHeading.removeEventListener('blur', handler);
    });
  }
}
```

## 5. Cognitive Load Mitigation

DFIR analysts during incident response experience significant cognitive fatigue during 12-16 hour shifts. All surfaces must minimize unnecessary mental overhead.

### 5.1 Progressive Disclosure in HTML Reports

Triage reports can contain thousands of evidence entries across 12 questions. Progressive disclosure prevents cognitive overload:

```html
<details class="triage-card">
  <summary>
    <h3>Were files securely deleted?</h3>
    <span class="severity-badge severity-critical" role="img" aria-label="Critical severity">
      <svg aria-hidden="true"><!-- shield-alert icon --></svg>
      CRITICAL
    </span>
    <span class="answer-text">YES (3 evidence entries)</span>
  </summary>
  <div class="triage-detail">
    <table role="table" aria-label="Evidence for question: were files securely deleted">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">#</th>
          <th scope="col">Timestamp</th>
          <th scope="col">Operation</th>
          <th scope="col">File Path</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <!-- Evidence rows -->
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</details>
```

Benefits:
- Analyst scans all 12 questions in seconds (badges only)
- Expands only the findings that matter to the current investigation
- Reduces visual noise during high-pressure triage

### 5.2 Time Expectation Setting

The ~35-second triage pipeline provides clear progress expectations across all surfaces:

**CLI:**
```
Triage starting... (estimated: ~35 seconds)
[1/7] Mounting evidence image...          done (2.1s)
[2/7] Parsing USN journal...              done (8.4s)
[3/7] Recovering ghost records...         done (5.2s)
[4/7] Scanning unallocated space...       done (11.3s)
[5/7] Reconstructing file paths...        done (3.1s)
[6/7] Running triage questions...         done (4.8s)
[7/7] Generating report...               done (0.3s)

Triage complete in 35.2 seconds.
```

**Enterprise web UI:**
```html
<div role="progressbar"
     aria-valuemin="0"
     aria-valuemax="7"
     aria-valuenow="3"
     aria-label="Triage progress: step 3 of 7, recovering ghost records">
  <div class="progress-track">
    <div class="progress-fill" style="width: 42.8%"></div>
  </div>
  <p class="progress-label">
    Step 3 of 7: Recovering ghost records
    <span class="progress-estimate">~20 seconds remaining</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

### 5.4 No Flashing or Blinking Elements

The report and web UI contain zero flashing or blinking elements. The `CRITICAL` badge uses a static bold red border, never a pulsing animation. The WebSocket connection indicator uses a static icon with text label, not a pulsing dot. This protects against photosensitive seizures and reduces distraction during long analysis sessions.

### 5.5 Consistent Layout

- Triage cards always appear in the same order (the 12 questions are deterministic)
- Stat cards maintain fixed positions: Total, Carved, Ghost, Alerts (left to right)
- Tab order (Story, Explore) never changes
- Enterprise dashboard nav order is fixed across all views
- No content reflows unexpectedly after initial render

### 6.2 Form Validation and Error Handling

```html
<!-- Error summary at top of form (focus target on validation failure) -->
<div
  id="form-errors"
  role="alert"
  aria-label="Form validation errors"
  tabindex="-1"
  hidden>
  <h3>Please correct the following errors:</h3>
  <ul>
    <!-- Populated by JavaScript; links to individual fields -->
  </ul>
</div>
```

```javascript
function onFormValidationFail(errors) {
  var errorSummary = document.getElementById('form-errors');
  var errorList = errorSummary.querySelector('ul');
  errorList.innerHTML = '';

  errors.forEach(function(err) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    var link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = '#' + err.fieldId;
    link.textContent = err.fieldLabel + ': ' + err.message;
    li.appendChild(link);
    errorList.appendChild(li);
  });

  // Show and focus error summary
  errorSummary.hidden = false;
  errorSummary.focus();

  // Mark individual fields
  errors.forEach(function(err) {
    var field = document.getElementById(err.fieldId);
    field.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    var errorEl = document.getElementById(err.fieldId + '-error');
    if (!errorEl) {
      errorEl = document.createElement('p');
      errorEl.id = err.fieldId + '-error';
      errorEl.className = 'form-error';
      errorEl.setAttribute('role', 'alert');
      field.parentNode.appendChild(errorEl);
    }
    errorEl.textContent = err.message;

    var describedBy = field.getAttribute('aria-describedby') || '';
    if (describedBy.indexOf(errorEl.id) === -1) {
      field.setAttribute('aria-describedby', (describedBy + ' ' + errorEl.id).trim());
    }
  });
}
```

## 7. Keyboard Navigation

### 7.1 HTML Report Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key | Action | Context |
|-----|--------|---------|
| `Tab` | Move to next focusable element | Global |
| `Shift+Tab` | Move to previous focusable element | Global |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activate tab or expand triage card | Tabs, cards |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Switch between Story and Explore tabs | Tab bar |
| `Escape` | Collapse expanded triage card detail | Triage cards |
| `/` | Focus search input (Explore tab) | Explore tab |
| `j` / `k` | Next/previous triage card | Story tab |

```javascript
// Embedded in HTML report <script>

// Tab switcher: Arrow keys to switch tabs
document.querySelector('[role="tablist"]').addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
  var tabs = Array.from(e.currentTarget.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]'));
  var currentIndex = tabs.indexOf(document.activeElement);
  var newIndex;

  switch (e.key) {
    case 'ArrowRight':
    case 'ArrowDown':
      newIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % tabs.length;
      break;
    case 'ArrowLeft':
    case 'ArrowUp':
      newIndex = (currentIndex - 1 + tabs.length) % tabs.length;
      break;
    case 'Home':
      newIndex = 0;
      break;
    case 'End':
      newIndex = tabs.length - 1;
      break;
    default:
      return;
  }

  e.preventDefault();
  tabs[newIndex].focus();
  tabs[newIndex].click();
});

// Data table: sortable columns via Enter/Space on th elements
document.querySelectorAll('th[aria-sort]').forEach(function(th) {
  th.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');
  th.setAttribute('role', 'columnheader');
  th.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      e.preventDefault();
      th.click();
    }
  });
});
```

### 7.2 Enterprise Web Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key | Action | Scope |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `?` | Show keyboard shortcuts help | Global |
| `/` | Focus case search | Global |
| `Escape` | Close modal / clear search | Global |
| `j` / `k` | Navigate findings list (down/up) | Findings panel |
| `Enter` | Open selected finding detail | Findings panel |
| `1`-`9` | Jump to triage question N | Results view |
| `e` | Toggle evidence panel | Results view |
| `n` | Add note to current finding | Results view |

```javascript
// enterprise/static/js/shortcuts.js

document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
  // Skip if user is in an input field
  if (['INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'SELECT'].indexOf(e.target.tagName) !== -1) return;
  if (e.target.isContentEditable) return;

  switch (e.key) {
    case '?':
      showShortcutsModal();
      break;
    case '/':
      e.preventDefault();
      document.getElementById('case-search').focus();
      break;
    case 'Escape':
      closeActiveModal();
      break;
  }
});
```

### 7.3 Focus Trap for Modals (Enterprise Web)

```javascript
// enterprise/static/js/modal.js

function trapFocus(modalElement) {
  var focusableSelectors = [
    'a[href]', 'button:not([disabled])', 'input:not([disabled])',
    'select:not([disabled])', 'textarea:not([disabled])',
    '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'
  ].join(', ');

  var focusable = modalElement.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
  var firstFocusable = focusable[0];
  var lastFocusable = focusable[focusable.length - 1];

  // Store trigger element to restore focus on close
  modalElement._triggerElement = document.activeElement;

  firstFocusable.focus();

  modalElement.addEventListener('keydown', function handler(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      closeModal(modalElement);
      return;
    }

    if (e.key !== 'Tab') return;

    if (e.shiftKey) {
      if (document.activeElement === firstFocusable) {
        e.preventDefault();
        lastFocusable.focus();
      }
    } else {
      if (document.activeElement === lastFocusable) {
        e.preventDefault();
        firstFocusable.focus();
      }
    }
  });
}

function closeModal(modalElement) {
  modalElement.hidden = true;
  modalElement.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');

  if (modalElement._triggerElement) {
    modalElement._triggerElement.focus();
  }
}
```

## 8. Component Accessibility Requirements

### 8.1 Required ARIA Patterns by Component

**Shared components (HTML report + enterprise web):**

| Component | ARIA Pattern | Key Attributes |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `severity_badge` | Status indicator | `role="img"`, `aria-label="{severity} severity"`, icon `aria-hidden="true"` |
| `evidence_card` | Card article | `role="article"`, heading-based structure, `aria-label` on container |
| `loading_states` | Progress indicator | `role="progressbar"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, text label |

**HTML report components:**

| Component | ARIA Pattern | Key Attributes |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `report_tab_switcher` | Tabs | `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` |
| `timeline_entry` | List item | Semantic `<li>` within `<ol>`, timestamp in `<time>`, operation as text |
| `data_table` | Table | `<table>` with `<thead>`, `<th scope="col">`, `aria-sort` on sortable columns |
| `sparkline` | Image | `role="img"`, `aria-label` with text summary ("Activity peak at 14:23, 847 events") |
| `stat_card` | Group | `role="group"`, `aria-label="Label: Value"` |
| `triage_card` | Article | `role="article"`, `aria-label`, expandable with `aria-expanded` |
| `triage_badge` | Status | `role="status"`, `aria-label="Answer: X, confidence Y"` |

**Enterprise web components:**

| Component | ARIA Pattern | Key Attributes |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| `buttons` | Button | Native `<button>`, `aria-disabled` (not `disabled` to keep focusable), loading state announced |
| `case_status_badge` | Status | `role="status"`, text label + icon, color-blind safe (Section 9) |
| `input_fields` | Form input | `<label>`, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` for hints/errors |
| `dashboard_card` | Region | `role="region"`, `aria-label`, heading-based internal structure |
| `analyst_avatar` | Image | `alt="{analyst_name}"`, presence indicator as text ("Online"/"Offline"), not color-only |
| `audit_trail_entry` | Log entry | Within `role="log"`, timestamped, action description in text |
| `rbac_navigation` | Navigation | `<nav aria-label="Main navigation">`, `aria-current="page"` on active item |
| `websocket_indicator` | Status | `role="status"`, text label: "Connected" / "Disconnected" / "Reconnecting" |
| `pipeline_progress` | Progressbar | `role="progressbar"`, step counter, stage label, time estimate |
| `skeleton_loader` | Loading placeholder | `aria-busy="true"` on container, `aria-label="Loading {content_type}"` |
| `search_input` | Search | `<label>`, `aria-describedby` for hints, result count via `aria-live` region |
| `filter_controls` | Toolbar | `role="toolbar"`, `aria-label` on each filter, changes via `aria-live` |

### 8.2 Focus Indicator Specification

All interactive elements receive the standard focus ring (defined in Section 4.5).

## 9. Color-Blind Safe Severity Indicators

Severity levels must never rely solely on color. All three surfaces use a multi-channel encoding strategy: color + icon/symbol + text label + border pattern.

### 9.1 Multi-Channel Severity Encoding

| Severity | Color (Dark) | Color (Light) | Icon (Lucide) | Text Label | CLI Symbol | Badge Style |
|----------|-------------|---------------|---------------|------------|------------|-------------|
| Critical | #ff7b72 | #cf222e | `ShieldAlert` | CRITICAL | `[!!]` | Solid fill |
| High | #ffa657 | #bc4c00 | `AlertTriangle` | HIGH | `[!]` | Solid fill |
| Medium | #d29922 | #7d4e00 | `AlertCircle` | MEDIUM | `[~]` | Outline |
| Low | #58a6ff | #0550ae | `Info` | LOW | `[-]` | Outline |
| Info | #8b949e | #57606a | `MessageCircle` | INFO | `[.]` | No badge |
| Ghost | #bc8cff | #6639ba | `Ghost` | GHOST | `[G]` | Dashed outline |

### 9.2 HTML/Web Severity Badge Implementation

```html
<!-- Severity badge: color + icon + text (never color alone) -->
<span class="severity-badge severity-critical" role="img" aria-label="Critical severity">
  <svg class="severity-icon" aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16">
    <use href="#icon-shield-alert" />
  </svg>
  <span class="severity-text">CRITICAL</span>
</span>
```

```css
.severity-badge {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.25rem;
  padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem;
  border-radius: 4px;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

/* Solid fill for critical + high (demands attention) */
.severity-critical {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, #ff7b72 20%, transparent);
  color: #ff7b72;
  border: 1px solid #ff7b72;
}
.severity-high {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, #ffa657 20%, transparent);
  color: #ffa657;
  border: 1px solid #ffa657;
}

/* Outline for medium + low (informational) */
.severity-medium {
  background: transparent;
  color: #d29922;
  border: 1px solid #d29922;
}
.severity-low {
  background: transparent;
  color: #58a6ff;
  border: 1px solid #58a6ff;

/* Text only for info */
.severity-info {
  background: transparent;
  color: #8b949e;
  border: 1px solid transparent;

  color: #bc8cff;
```

### 9.3 CLI Severity (NO_COLOR Mode)

When color is unavailable, severity is communicated through text labels and ASCII symbols:

```
[!!] CRITICAL: Endpoint protection disabled (3 entries)
[!]  HIGH:     Suspicious PowerShell execution (7 entries)
[~]  MEDIUM:   USB device connected during incident window (2 entries)
[-]  LOW:      Standard software installation (12 entries)
[.]  INFO:     Normal user file operations (847 entries)
[G]  GHOST:    Recovered deleted antivirus log entries (14 entries)
```

### 9.4 Color-Blind Simulation Verification

The design system must be verified under the three most common color vision deficiencies:

| Deficiency | Prevalence | Risk | Mitigation |
|------------|-----------|------|------------|
| Protanopia (no red) | ~1% male | Critical/High may look similar | Different icons (ShieldAlert vs AlertTriangle) + text labels + solid vs solid fill |
| Deuteranopia (no green) | ~6% male | Success/warning may blur | Success uses checkmark icon + "COMPLETE" text |
| Tritanopia (no blue) | ~0.01% | Low severity may lose contrast | Low uses Info icon + text + outline border |

All severity indicators remain distinguishable via icon shape + text label + border pattern (solid/outline/dashed) even with complete color blindness (achromatopsia).

## 10. Testing Protocol

### 10.1 Automated Testing

**CLI accessibility tests (Rust integration tests):**

```rust
// tests/cli_accessibility.rs

#[test]
fn test_no_color_strips_ansi() {
    let output = Command::new("katana")
        .arg("triage")
        .arg("tests/fixtures/small.E01")
        .env("NO_COLOR", "1")
        .output()
        .expect("Failed to run katana");

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    assert!(!stdout.contains('\x1b'), "Output contains ANSI escapes with NO_COLOR set");
    assert!(stdout.contains("[CRITICAL]") || stdout.contains("[HIGH]"),
        "Text severity labels missing in NO_COLOR mode");
}

#[test]
fn test_pipe_strips_ansi() {
    let output = Command::new("katana")
        .arg("triage")
        .arg("tests/fixtures/small.E01")
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .output()
        .expect("Failed to run katana");

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    assert!(!stdout.contains('\x1b'), "Output contains ANSI escapes when piped");
}

#[test]
fn test_term_dumb_strips_ansi() {
    let output = Command::new("katana")
        .arg("triage")
        .arg("tests/fixtures/small.E01")
        .env("TERM", "dumb")
        .output()
        .expect("Failed to run katana");

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    assert!(!stdout.contains('\x1b'), "Output contains ANSI escapes with TERM=dumb");
}

#[test]
fn test_severity_labels_always_present() {
    let output = Command::new("katana")
        .arg("triage")
        .arg("tests/fixtures/small.E01")
        .env_remove("NO_COLOR")
        .output()
        .expect("Failed to run katana");

    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
    let has_severity = stdout.contains("CRITICAL") ||
                       stdout.contains("HIGH") ||
                       stdout.contains("MEDIUM") ||
                       stdout.contains("LOW") ||
                       stdout.contains("INFO");
    assert!(has_severity, "Severity text labels missing from output");
}
```

### 10.2 Manual Testing Checklist

| Test | CLI | HTML Report | Enterprise Web | Pass Criteria |
|------|-----|-------------|----------------|---------------|
| **NO_COLOR compliance** | `NO_COLOR=1 katana triage img.E01` | N/A | N/A | Zero ANSI escapes in output |
| **Pipe detection** | `katana triage img.E01 \| cat` | N/A | N/A | Clean text, no escape codes |
| **TERM=dumb** | `TERM=dumb katana triage img.E01` | N/A | N/A | No progress bar, line-by-line status |
| **Keyboard navigation** | Inherent (CLI) | Tab through all interactive elements | Tab through entire dashboard | All elements reachable, logical order |
| **Screen reader (VoiceOver)** | Run in Terminal.app with VoiceOver | Open in Safari with VoiceOver | Full dashboard walkthrough | All content announced, live regions work |
| **Screen reader (NVDA)** | N/A | Open in Firefox with NVDA | Full dashboard walkthrough with NVDA | Same as VoiceOver criteria |
| **Zoom 200%** | N/A (terminal font) | Browser zoom | Browser zoom | No horizontal scroll, content readable |
| **Zoom 400%** | N/A | Browser zoom | Browser zoom | Content reflows, no loss of function |
| **Reduced motion** | N/A | Set `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | Set preference | No animations, progress still visible |
| **High contrast** | N/A (text-based) | Windows High Contrast mode | Windows High Contrast mode | Content visible, focus rings visible |
| **Color alone** | Use `--no-color` | Apply grayscale CSS filter | Apply grayscale filter | All severity levels distinguishable |
| **Dark/light mode** | N/A (terminal theme) | Toggle `prefers-color-scheme` | Toggle preference | Contrast ratios maintained in both |
| **Data table scrolling** | N/A | Resize to < 600px | Resize to < 600px | Tables scrollable, announced to SR |
| **Print preview** | N/A | Browser print preview | N/A | Light theme, badges readable, no interactive elements |

### 10.3 Screen Reader Test Scripts

#### HTML Report (VoiceOver + Safari)

```markdown
### Report Load
1. Open triage.html in Safari
2. Enable VoiceOver (Cmd+F5)
3. Verify: Page title announced ("Triage Report: {case_name} - Security Ronin Katana")
4. Verify: Skip link available ("Skip to triage results")
5. Verify: Landmark regions announced (banner, main, contentinfo)

### Stat Cards
1. Navigate to stat cards group
2. Verify: "Key metrics, group" announced
3. Tab through each card
4. Verify: Each announces "Total Records: 142,847" (label + value together)

### Tab Navigation
1. Navigate to tab bar
2. Verify: "Report views, tab list" announced
3. Verify: "Story, selected, tab, 1 of 2" announced
4. Press ArrowRight
5. Verify: "Explore, tab, 2 of 2" announced and panel switches

### Triage Cards (Story Tab)
1. Navigate into Story tab content
2. Verify: Each triage card announces question text
3. Verify: Badge announces severity and answer ("Critical severity", "Answer: Yes")
4. Verify: Expanding card announces supporting evidence table
5. Verify: Table headers announced for evidence rows

### Explore Tab
1. Switch to Explore tab
2. Verify: "USN Journal records, region" announced
3. Verify: Search input has label announced
4. Type a filter term
5. Verify: "Showing N of M records" announced via live region
6. Navigate table
7. Verify: Column headers associated with cell data
```

#### Enterprise Web (NVDA + Firefox)

```markdown
### Dashboard Load
1. Navigate to enterprise dashboard
2. Verify: Page title announced ("{page} - {case_name} - Katana Enterprise")
3. Verify: Skip links available (main content, case list, triage results)
4. Verify: WebSocket connection status announced ("Connected" via status role)

### Case List
1. Navigate to case list
2. Verify: Case list announced with count
3. Use j/k to navigate cases
4. Verify: Case name, status, and severity announced per case
5. Press Enter to open case
6. Verify: Focus moves to case heading

### Real-Time Collaboration
1. Have another analyst add a finding (or simulate via test harness)
2. Verify: Collaboration update announced politely (not interrupting current task)
3. Verify: Multiple rapid updates are coalesced (not one announcement per second)

### Triage Pipeline
1. Start triage on a case
2. Verify: Button state changes to disabled, announced
3. Verify: Progress updates announced (at most once per 5 seconds)
4. Wait for completion
5. Verify: "Triage complete for case {id}. N findings, M critical." announced assertively
6. Verify: Focus moves to results heading

### Form Validation
1. Submit case creation form with empty required fields
2. Verify: Error summary announced ("Please correct the following errors")
3. Verify: Focus moves to error summary
4. Verify: Individual field errors announced when navigating to fields
5. Fix errors and resubmit
6. Verify: Success state announced
```

## 11. Font Scaling and Responsive Design

### 11.1 Browser Zoom Support

```css
html {
  font-size: 100%; /* Inherits user preference (typically 16px) */
}

body {
  font-size: 0.8125rem; /* 13px at default, scales with user preference */
  line-height: 1.5;
}

/* All spacing uses rem or em */
.triage-card { padding: 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; }
.stat-card { padding: 1rem; }
.container {
  max-width: 72rem;
  width: 100%;
  padding: 0 1rem;
}
```

### 11.2 Responsive Breakpoints

```css
/* Default: 4-column stat cards */
.stat-cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
  gap: 0.75rem;
}

/* Tablet / high zoom: 2 columns */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .stat-cards {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
  }
}

/* Mobile / very high zoom: single column */
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .stat-cards {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }

  /* Explore table scrolls horizontally with keyboard access */
  .table-wrapper {
    overflow-x: auto;
    -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
  }
  .table-wrapper[tabindex="0"]:focus {
    outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #58a6ff);
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }
}
```

# Security Ronin Katana: UI Design System

# Security Ronin Katana: UI Design System

> **Parent**: [../BRAND_GUIDELINES.md](../BRAND_GUIDELINES.md)
> **Created**: 2026-03-10
> **Status**: Active
> **Generation Step**: 5b of 13 -- Requires `brand.colors`, `brand.typography`, `journeys.*`

Production-ready design tokens, ANSI escape sequences, CSS configuration, and component specifications for Katana's three rendering surfaces: CLI terminal output, HTML reports, and enterprise web UI.

## Document Purpose

This document provides **copy-paste ready code** for implementing Security Ronin Katana's visual design across all three interface surfaces. It contains:

1. ANSI color codes and terminal formatting rules (CLI output)
2. CSS custom properties / design tokens (HTML reports and enterprise web)
3. Framework integration patterns (Axum + Askama templates, vanilla CSS)
4. Component specifications per surface (CLI, HTML report, enterprise web)
5. Utility classes and responsive patterns (enterprise web only)

**Relationship to Other Documents:**
- **BRAND_GUIDELINES.md** defines the rationale, voice, and constraints
- **USER_JOURNEYS.md** defines the user flows these surfaces serve
- **This document** defines the implementation tokens and component specs

**Three Rendering Surfaces:**

| Surface | Tier | Technology | Primary Users |
|---------|------|------------|---------------|
| CLI terminal output | Community + Enterprise | Rust `colored` crate, ANSI escapes | All analysts |
| HTML report | Community + Enterprise | Static HTML/CSS/JS (generated by Rust) | Analysts reviewing triage results |
| Enterprise web UI | Enterprise only | Axum + Askama + vanilla CSS + WebSocket | MSSP teams, enterprise IR |

## 1. CLI Terminal Design Tokens

### 1.1 ANSI Color Mapping

Katana uses the `colored` crate for terminal output. All colors map to standard ANSI 256 palette for maximum terminal compatibility.

```rust
// katana/src/output/colors.rs

/// Severity-level colors for triage output
pub mod severity {
    pub const CRITICAL: &str = "\x1b[1;91m";  // Bold bright red
    pub const HIGH: &str     = "\x1b[91m";     // Bright red
    pub const MEDIUM: &str   = "\x1b[93m";     // Bright yellow
    pub const LOW: &str      = "\x1b[96m";     // Bright cyan
    pub const INFO: &str     = "\x1b[37m";     // White
    pub const RESET: &str    = "\x1b[0m";
}

/// Structural element colors
pub mod structure {
    pub const HEADER: &str     = "\x1b[1;97m"; // Bold bright white
    pub const SUBHEADER: &str  = "\x1b[1;36m"; // Bold cyan
    pub const LABEL: &str      = "\x1b[90m";   // Dark gray
    pub const VALUE: &str      = "\x1b[37m";   // White
    pub const PATH: &str       = "\x1b[33m";   // Yellow (file paths)
    pub const TIMESTAMP: &str  = "\x1b[34m";   // Blue (timestamps)
    pub const COUNT: &str      = "\x1b[1;32m"; // Bold green (numeric counts)
    pub const HASH: &str       = "\x1b[35m";   // Magenta (SHA-256, hashes)
    pub const SEPARATOR: &str  = "\x1b[90m";   // Dark gray (lines, borders)
    pub const RESET: &str      = "\x1b[0m";
}

/// Progress and pipeline stage indicators
pub mod progress {
    pub const ACTIVE: &str   = "\x1b[1;96m";  // Bold bright cyan
    pub const DONE: &str     = "\x1b[32m";     // Green
    pub const PENDING: &str  = "\x1b[90m";     // Dark gray
    pub const ERROR: &str    = "\x1b[1;91m";   // Bold bright red
    pub const SPINNER: &[char] = &['|', '/', '-', '\\'];
}
```

### 1.2 CLI Typography Rules

```
Terminal Assumptions:
- Minimum width: 80 columns
- Recommended width: 120 columns
- Font: User's terminal font (monospace by definition)
- Encoding: UTF-8 (box-drawing characters allowed)

Text Hierarchy:
- Section headers:  UPPERCASE, bold white, preceded by blank line
- Sub-headers:      Title Case, bold cyan
- Labels:           dark gray, right-aligned to column width, followed by colon
- Values:           white, left-aligned after label
- Emphasis:         bold (never italic -- terminals vary)
```

### 1.3 CLI Table Formatting

```
Column Rules:
- Minimum column width: 4 characters
- Column separator: " | " (space-pipe-space) in dark gray
- Header separator: "---+---" repeated (dark gray)
- Number columns: right-aligned
- Text columns: left-aligned
- Truncation: "..." suffix when content exceeds column width
- Maximum table width: terminal width minus 2

Example Output:
  TRIAGE RESULTS
  Question                          | Answer  | Confidence | Evidence
  ----------------------------------+---------+------------+---------
  Ransomware activity detected?     | YES     | HIGH       | 47 hits
  Data exfiltration indicators?     | NO      | MEDIUM     | 0 hits
  Lateral movement observed?        | YES     | HIGH       | 12 hits
```

### 1.4 CLI Progress Bar

```
Pipeline Stage Visualization:

  [Parse]---->[Correlate]---->[Triage]---->[Report]
    Done        Active         Pending      Pending

Single-line progress (for each stage):
  Parsing USN Journal... [=========>          ] 47% (1.2M / 2.6M records)

Streaming phase output:
  [1/4] Parsing USN Journal............ 2,614,831 records (1.2s)
  [2/4] Correlating MFT paths.......... 2,614,831 resolved (0.8s)
  [3/4] Running triage questions....... 12/12 complete (0.3s)
  [4/4] Generating report.............. report.html (0.1s)

  Total: 2.4s | Ghost recoveries: 1,847 | Triage hits: 127
```

### 1.5 CLI Error Formatting

```
Error Pattern (always to stderr):

  ERROR: <one-line description>

  Cause:  <technical detail>
  Fix:    <actionable next step>

  Exit code: <1 or 2>

Example:
  ERROR: Unsupported filesystem type: ext4

  Cause:  Katana supports NTFS only. Detected ext4 on partition 2.
  Fix:    Verify the image contains an NTFS volume.
         Supported: NTFS (MBR, GPT, E01, raw)

  Exit code: 2

Warning Pattern (always to stderr):
  WARN: <one-line description> -- <consequence or fallback>

Example:
  WARN: USN Journal not found -- falling back to unallocated carving only
```

### 1.6 CLI Color Disable Rules

```rust
// Color output MUST be disabled when:
// 1. stdout is not a TTY (piped to file or another command)
// 2. NO_COLOR environment variable is set (https://no-color.org)
// 3. --no-color flag is passed
// 4. TERM=dumb
//
// Detection order:
//   if args.no_color || env::var("NO_COLOR").is_ok() || !atty::is(Stream::Stdout) {
//       colored::control::set_override(false);
//   }
```

```css
  --z-modal-backdrop: 40;
  --z-modal: 50;
  --z-popover: 60;
  --z-tooltip: 70;

  /* =========================
     FOCUS & ACCESSIBILITY
     ========================= */

  --ring: #58a6ff;
  --ring-offset: 2px;
}

/* Reduced motion preference */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root {
    --transition-fast: 0ms;
    --transition-base: 0ms;
    --transition-slow: 0ms;
    --transition-slower: 0ms;
  }
}
```

## 3. Framework Integration

### 3.1 Technology Stack Per Surface

| Surface | Renderer | CSS Approach | Template Engine |
|---------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| CLI | Rust `colored` crate | N/A (ANSI escapes) | Hardcoded format strings |
| HTML Report | Rust binary generates static HTML | Vanilla CSS (embedded in `<style>`) | `askama` or string templates |
| Enterprise Web | Axum server | Vanilla CSS (external stylesheet) | `askama` templates |

### 3.2 HTML Report Integration

The HTML report is a single self-contained `.html` file generated by the Katana binary. All CSS is embedded inline within `<style>` tags. No external dependencies.

```rust
// katana/src/output/html.rs -- Structure
//
// The CSS custom properties from Section 2 are embedded verbatim
// into the <style> block of every generated report.
//
// Template structure:
//   <html>
//     <head>
//       <style>/* Section 2 tokens + Section 4 component CSS */</style>
//       <script>/* Tab switching + DataTables init */</script>
//     </head>
//     <body>
//       <nav><!-- Story | Explore tab switcher --></nav>
//       <main id="story"><!-- Narrative timeline --></main>
//       <main id="explore"><!-- Interactive data tables --></main>
//     </body>
//   </html>
```

### 3.3 Enterprise Web Integration (Axum + Askama)

```rust
// enterprise/src/web/templates.rs -- Structure
//
// Askama templates reference the CSS custom properties.
// Static CSS file served from /static/katana.css
//
// Route structure:
//   GET  /                    -> Dashboard
//   GET  /cases/:id           -> Case detail
//   GET  /cases/:id/timeline  -> Timeline view
//   GET  /cases/:id/evidence  -> Evidence explorer
//   WS   /ws/cases/:id        -> Real-time updates
//   GET  /static/katana.css   -> Design system CSS
```

### 3.4 Token Mapping Across Surfaces

| Semantic Purpose | CLI (ANSI) | HTML/Web (CSS) |
|-----------------|------------|----------------|
| Critical finding | `\x1b[1;91m` (bold bright red) | `var(--color-critical)` #ff4757 |
| High severity | `\x1b[91m` (bright red) | `var(--color-high)` #ff6b6b |
| Warning/medium | `\x1b[93m` (bright yellow) | `var(--color-warning)` #d29922 |
| Success/clean | `\x1b[32m` (green) | `var(--color-success)` #3fb950 |
| Informational | `\x1b[37m` (white) | `var(--color-info)` #58a6ff |
| Ghost recovery | `\x1b[35m` (magenta) | `var(--color-ghost)` #bc8cff |
| File path | `\x1b[33m` (yellow) | `var(--color-warning)` with `font-mono` |
| Timestamp | `\x1b[34m` (blue) | `var(--color-accent)` with `font-mono` |
| Muted/label | `\x1b[90m` (dark gray) | `var(--color-text-muted)` |
| Hash/checksum | `\x1b[35m` (magenta) | `var(--color-ghost)` with `font-mono` |

### 3.5 Configuration Structure

```yaml
# Pseudocode -- adapt to Axum/Askama or Rust template engine

ThemeConfig:
  colors:
    background: var(--color-background)       # #0d1117
    surface: var(--color-surface)             # #161b22
    accent:
      default: var(--color-accent)            # #58a6ff
      hover: var(--color-accent-hover)        # #79b8ff
      subtle: var(--color-accent-subtle)      # rgba(88,166,255,0.15)
    text:
      primary: var(--color-text-primary)      # #e6edf3
      secondary: var(--color-text-secondary)  # #9da5b4
      muted: var(--color-text-muted)          # #545d68
    border:
      default: var(--color-border)            # #30363d
      strong: var(--color-border-strong)      # #484f58
    severity:
      critical: var(--color-critical)         # #ff4757
      high: var(--color-high)                 # #ff6b6b
      warning: var(--color-warning)           # #d29922
      success: var(--color-success)           # #3fb950
      info: var(--color-info)                 # #58a6ff
      ghost: var(--color-ghost)               # #bc8cff

  typography:
    fontFamily:
      display: var(--font-display)            # Inter, system-ui
      body: var(--font-body)                  # Inter, system-ui
      mono: var(--font-mono)                  # JetBrains Mono, Fira Code

  animations:
    fadeIn: opacity 0 -> 1, 200ms
    fadeUp: opacity 0 -> 1 + translateY 8px -> 0, 200ms
    pulseSubtle: opacity 1 -> 0.4 -> 1, 1s infinite
```

## 4. Component Specifications

### 4.1 Severity Badge

Used across all three surfaces to indicate triage finding severity.

**CLI:**
```
  [CRITICAL]  Ransomware activity detected
  [HIGH]      Lateral movement observed
  [MEDIUM]    Suspicious scheduled task
  [LOW]       Uncommon executable path
  [INFO]      Normal system activity
```

**CSS (HTML Report + Enterprise Web):**
```css
.badge-severity {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  padding: var(--space-0-5) var(--space-2);
  border-radius: var(--radius-full);
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--text-xs);
  font-weight: var(--font-semibold);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

.badge-critical {
  background-color: var(--color-critical-subtle);
  color: var(--color-critical);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-critical);
}

.badge-high {
  background-color: var(--color-high-subtle);
  color: var(--color-high);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-high);
}

.badge-medium {
  background-color: var(--color-warning-subtle);
  color: var(--color-warning);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-warning);
}

.badge-low {
  background-color: var(--color-info-subtle);
  color: var(--color-info);
  border: 1px solid var(--color-info);
}

.badge-info {
  background-color: var(--color-surface-elevated);

  border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
}

.badge-ghost {
  background-color: var(--color-ghost-subtle);
```

```css
}
```

## 6. Responsive Breakpoints (Enterprise Web Only)

The CLI and HTML report are not responsive -- CLI fills the terminal width, and the HTML report targets desktop browser viewing during analysis sessions. The enterprise web UI supports tablet and desktop viewports.

### 6.1 Standard Breakpoints

| Name | Width | Use Case |
|------|-------|----------|
| `md` | 768px | Tablet -- case list or detail, single column |
| `lg` | 1024px | Laptop -- sidebar visible + content area |
| `xl` | 1280px | Desktop -- sidebar + content + evidence panel |
| `2xl` | 1536px | Wide monitor -- full three-column layout |

No mobile breakpoint. Forensic analysis is not performed on phones.

### 6.2 Enterprise Layout Patterns

```css
/* Main layout: sidebar + content */
.layout-main {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr;
  min-height: 100vh;
}

/* Case detail: content + evidence panel */
@media (min-width: 1280px) {
  .layout-case-detail {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 400px;
    gap: var(--space-4);
  }
}

/* Dashboard grid */
.dashboard-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
  gap: var(--space-4);
}

@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .dashboard-grid {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
  }
}

/* Case list responsive */
.case-list {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  gap: var(--space-3);
}

@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .case-list {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
  }
}

@media (min-width: 1536px) {
  .case-list {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  }
}
```

## 9. Accessibility Integration

This document provides **visual tokens and CSS implementation**. For comprehensive accessibility guidance, see ACCESSIBILITY.md when generated.

### 9.1 Coverage Matrix

| Concern | CLI | HTML Report | Enterprise Web |
|---------|-----|-------------|----------------|
| **Color contrast** | ANSI colors on dark/light terminal backgrounds | CSS token definitions (Section 2) | CSS token definitions (Section 2) |
| **Non-color indicators** | Severity text labels `[CRITICAL]` always present | Severity badges include text, not just color | Status dots paired with text labels |
| **Focus states** | N/A (no interactive elements) | Tab switcher focus ring | All interactive elements (Section 5.3) |
| **Reduced motion** | N/A | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query |
| **Screen readers** | N/A (terminal handles this) | Semantic HTML (`<nav>`, `<main>`, `<table>`) | Semantic HTML, ARIA labels on dynamic content |
| **Keyboard navigation** | N/A | Tab between Story/Explore tabs | Full keyboard nav, skip links |
| **Color-blind safe** | Severity always has text label alongside color | Severity always has text label alongside color | Status always has text label alongside color |

### 9.2 Required Accessibility Tokens

```css
/* Focus ring -- 5.2:1 contrast against --color-background (#0d1117) */
--ring: #58a6ff;
--ring-offset: 2px;

/* Error states -- never rely on color alone.
   Always pair with icon (AlertTriangle) + descriptive text. */
--color-error: #f85149;
--color-error-subtle: rgba(248, 81, 73, 0.15);
```

### 9.3 Cross-Reference Checklist

- [x] Color tokens pass WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI) -- `#e6edf3` on `#0d1117` = 13.2:1
- [x] Focus ring color has 3:1 contrast against all backgrounds -- `#58a6ff` on `#0d1117` = 5.2:1
- [x] Reduced motion tokens set transitions to 0ms
- [x] Component specs include focus state definitions
- [x] Loading states have non-motion alternatives (skeleton with `prefers-reduced-motion` falls back to static)
- [x] Severity indicators never rely on color alone (text labels always present)

## Quick Copy Reference

### CLI Output Patterns

```rust
// Triage result line
println!("{}{:<40}{} | {}{:<8}{} | {}{:<10}{} | {}{}{}",
    structure::LABEL, question, structure::RESET,
    severity_color, answer, severity::RESET,
    structure::LABEL, confidence, structure::RESET,
    structure::COUNT, evidence_count, structure::RESET,
);

// Error to stderr
eprintln!("{}ERROR:{} {}", severity::CRITICAL, severity::RESET, message);
eprintln!();
eprintln!("{}Cause:{}  {}", structure::LABEL, structure::RESET, cause);
eprintln!("{}Fix:{}    {}", structure::LABEL, structure::RESET, fix);
eprintln!();
eprintln!("Exit code: {}", exit_code);
```

### CSS Token Usage

```css
/* Dark page background */
background-color: var(--color-background);    /* #0d1117 */

/* Card/panel surface */
background-color: var(--color-surface);       /* #161b22 */

/* Primary text */
color: var(--color-text-primary);             /* #e6edf3 */

/* Monospace data (timestamps, paths, hex) */
font-family: var(--font-mono);

/* Clean UI text (headers, labels, buttons) */
font-family: var(--font-display);

/* Ghost recovery highlight */
background-color: var(--color-ghost-subtle);
color: var(--color-ghost);

/* Severity border on evidence cards */
border-left-color: var(--color-critical);     /* Critical findings */
border-left-color: var(--color-ghost);        /* Ghost recoveries */
```
